investigation.title: Flame Extinguishment Experiment
investigation.hardware: Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR)-Fluids and Combustion Facility (FCF), Multi-user Droplet Combustion Appartatus (MDCA)
investigation.objective: The FLEX (Flame Extinguishment Experiment) investigation aims to map the flammability limits of liquid fuels in microgravity environments, measure the effectiveness of various gaseous fire suppressants such as CO2, He, and SF6, and develop reliable predictive models for combustion limits under reduced gravity conditions. The mission seeks to validate and improve simplified models by incorporating detailed chemical reactions, heat transfer, and material movement, using both space-based data and extensive ground-based tests. Key flight experiment goals include obtaining high-resolution measurements of droplet burning rates, flame extinction behavior, heat radiation, soot levels, and temperature profiles, while systematically analyzing the effects of different ambient conditions and suppressant concentrations. These investigations are essential for advancing the fundamental understanding of combustion processes in microgravity and enhancing fire safety protocols for future space missions.

crew_environments.justification: Flown on the ISS; documents discuss CO2 extinguishers used in US ISS modules.
Research area is spacecraft fire safety; Shuttle extinguishers are discussed as current practice.
Tests at 30-34% O2 and about 71 kPa sit at the planned Moon-base cabin conditions from the challenge brief. Documents do not name a lunar base.
Same reduced-pressure, raised-O2 conditions as the Moon base. Documents also mention high-O2 EVA pre-breathe atmospheres.

evidence.text: Quantify the efficacy of gaseous suppressants (CO2, He, SF6) over candidate pressures and O2 levels.
Map flammability boundaries and the limiting oxygen index (LOI) of liquid fuels in reduced gravity.
evidence.source: FLEX_EIRD_v4.pdf (FLEX Research Requirements Document, 2005) p. 28; PSI-69_metadata (i_Investigation.txt) Approach

evidence.text: Extinction droplet diameter as a function of pressure, oxygen and suppressant.
Flammability boundaries and LOI as a function of pressure for the test fuels.
Burning rate, flame radiation, soot volume fraction and temperature.
Soot measured; soot escaping the flame is described as a long-term crew health hazard.

fuel.geometry: Single droplets, fiber-supported or free, tested initial diameter 1.1-4.7 mm

evidence.text: oxygen mole fraction shall range from 0.1-0.4
Target flow 0.1-5 cm/s for a subset of tests (droplet translated); most tests quiescent. Not recorded per test in the table.
Burning rate column; droplet size history from backlit view.
evidence.source: PSI-69_Experimental_table_FLEX.csv; FLEX_EIRD_v4.pdf (FLEX Research Requirements Document, 2005) p. 30

evidence.text: Visible flame extinction diameter and test outcome per test.
OH* imaging to capture flame size and thickness at extinction.

computed_findings.finding: Without suppressant at about 1 atm, flames generally went out at a larger fraction of the initial droplet size as oxygen dropped (not strictly monotonic for methanol).
computed_findings.method: Mean (extinction diameter / initial diameter) per fuel and O2 level, tests ending in 'Extinction', 95-108 kPa, no CO2/He.

computed_findings.finding: 24 tests ran at 30-34% O2; only 2 ended in extinction. 16 of them were at about 70-72 kPa, close to the planned Moon-base cabin pressure.
computed_findings.method: Filter x_o2 >= 0.30; Moon-base reference (>=30% O2, <=70.3 kPa) is from the Space Apps brief, not from FLEX documents.

computed_findings.finding: Diluent suppressants were tested up to 70% CO2 and 45% He; SF6 was planned but has no tests in this table.
computed_findings.source: PSI-69_Experimental_table_FLEX.csv; FLEX_EIRD_v4.pdf (FLEX Research Requirements Document, 2005) p. 38

computed_findings.finding: No CO2 or He suppressant tests were run above 25% O2, so suppressant data does not reach the 30%+ O2 range planned for lunar habitats.
computed_findings.method: Max x_o2 among tests with x_co2 > 0 or x_he > 0.

key_findings.finding: CO2, the current US ISS suppressant, is not physiologically inert at the concentrations needed to put out fires in microgravity, and its effectiveness there needed testing.
key_findings.fire_safety_relevance: Motivates evaluating alternative inert diluents (He) and the CO2 levels actually needed.

key_findings.finding: At high oxygen levels droplets tend to burn to completion instead of extinguishing, so extinction behavior must be mapped at low O2 down to the LOI.
key_findings.fire_safety_relevance: High-O2 cabins (EVA pre-breathe, planned lunar habitats) leave less margin before a fire self-extinguishes.

key_findings.finding: Low-pressure suppressant data were wanted because isolating a module and venting it to space is one firefighting strategy.
key_findings.fire_safety_relevance: Links depressurization response to measured extinction behavior at reduced pressure.

sources: FLEX_Overall_Ext_File-2.pdf (hardware handbook excerpts: CIR diagnostics, MDCA/FLEX-2 safety data)
notes: The Engineering Requirements Document is for FLEX-2, a separate follow-on investigation. It was not used for FLEX values.
FLEX_Overall_Ext_File-2.pdf is mostly rack hardware and imaging specs; used only to confirm diagnostics.
Burning-rate column is labelled 'mm' in the table; it is probably a burning-rate constant in mm^2/s. Check before displaying units.
Test 114 (C11M201) records 0 mmHg pressure; treated as missing. Some cells contain unreadable characters; treated as missing.
Extinction diameter of 0 treated as 'no measurable extinction diameter', not as a measurement.
Tested pressure starts at ~70 kPa although 0.5 atm was planned; SF6 was planned but not tested in this table.
Lunar Base and Pressurized Rover tags are inferred from conditions, not stated in FLEX documents.
